variables.reason: The problem defines Ra as "the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations" (arithmetic mean roughness). The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness uses the same symbol(s) (Ra, R_a) and explicitly defines it as the mean absolute deviation of surface height (first-order moment), with si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]. That record therefore directly applies to the problem variable Ra and supports the proposed SI exponent L=1. I also cite pq_equivalent_sandgrain_roughness because it documents related roughness-length quantities (ks) in the same domain, reinforcing that Ra is a dimensional length-scale used alongside ks in the referenced literature.

The candidate defines kt as "the peak-to-valley height, representing a length scale of surface roughness." The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height lists kt (and aliases Sx, k_t, k_c) as the mean peak-to-valley roughness height and states its si_dimension is L, matching the problem description. pq_mean_roughness_height is also cited as a related length-scale entry in the same dataset. These records show kt is dimensional with exponent L=1, supporting the proposed vector.

The problem names k_rms as the root-mean-square height of surface roughness. KB record pq_rms_roughness_height explicitly defines the root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean (symbols k_rms, krms) with si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]. That directly corresponds to the problem variable and confirms the length dimension (L=1) used in the candidate. pq_mean_roughness_height is cited as supporting contextual evidence that mean/scale heights are lengths in the same dataset.

The problem defines Sk as "the third central moment of roughness height fluctuations divided by the cube of their root-mean-square height," i.e. the standardized third moment (skewness). The KB record pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness (symbols Sk, S_k) as the third standardized moment and gives si_dimension 1 (dimensionless), supporting the proposed all-zero SI exponent vector. This record therefore directly applies to Sk in the original problem statement.

Ku is given as the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (Ku, K_u) as the fourth standardized moment with si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). This directly matches the problem variable and supports the candidate dimensionless SI exponents (all zeros).

The candidate lists ES as the effective streamwise slope of the roughness. KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines effective surface slope (symbols ES, E_x) as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction and explicitly notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and therefore dimensionless (si_dimension 1). That record directly applies to ES in the problem and supports the proposed all-zero SI exponent vector.

Po is given as surface porosity. The KB record pq_porosity (symbols Po, P_o, phi_p) defines porosity as a fraction of void or open volume/area and has si_dimension 1 (dimensionless). The definition aligns with the problem variable and supports the candidate dimensionless SI exponents (all zeros).

gate.entity_policy: Only Checker-selected visible record IDs identify cited canonical entities; no unselected-record or Analyzer-name anchor. Equal vectors do not establish equal physical entities.
gate.physical_correctness_scope: A passed contract is not a theorem of physical correctness. Record ID and coordinate checks establish citation consistency; semantic relevance/applicability in the reason and internal-reasoning physics remain model judgements.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness ks/Ra is dimensionless as it is a ratio of two lengths (ks and Ra). The input parameters include length scales (Ra, kt, k_rms) and dimensionless shape/statistical parameters (Sk, Ku, ES, Po). The dimensionless parameters have no physical dimensions, while the length scales have dimension of length. The output ks/Ra is dimensionless, consistent with the ratio of lengths.
